name: urho3d
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. Docs/Reference.dox (Containers page) says its own String/Vector/PODVector/HashMap give 'increased performance in some cases' versus STL, with no numbers, hardware or benchmark code; README makes no performance claim; no benchmark issues (issue search 'benchmark faster' returned only #1201 'Add Vulkan renderer' and #6). Repo archived 2023-01-25.

name: Video++
listed_description: A C++14 high performance video and image processing library.
reason: No published numbers in repo. README claims speed via meta-programming with no figures. benchmarks/ holds Google Benchmark sources (fast_detector.cc compares vpp fast9 against OpenCV FAST; box_filter.cc compares against naive and OpenMP loops; pyrlk_opencv_comparison.cc) but no results file, CPU or flags; fast_detector_draw_speedup.py reads a fast_lm_benchmark3.txt that is not in the repo. The only quantified claim is the DASIP 2014 paper abstract (seen only in WebSearch snippets: code up to 32x faster than naive equivalents), a hand-written naive loop baseline rather than a named library, and the PDF hosts (perso.ensta-paris.fr, hal) are unreachable here. Last commit 2019-02-07.

name: VIGRA
listed_description: A generic C++ computer vision library for image analysis.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README and docsrc/index.dxx only say templates let performance 'approach that of a traditional, hand tuned, inflexible, solution'; docsrc/image_processing.dxx says the old iterator APIs 'used to be considerably faster' than MultiArrayView (internal, no numbers); changelog mentions benchmarks by Paul Viola with no figures; no OpenCV comparison in issues; WebSearch found no third-party VIGRA vs OpenCV timings.

name: VLFeat
listed_description: The VLFeat open source library implements popular computer vision algorithms specialising in image understanding and local featurexs extraction and matching.
reason: README and headers carry no benchmark numbers (algorithm documentation lives on vlfeat.org, which is unreachable here). WebSearch surfaced a 2024 paper (eprints.uad.ac.id, PDF host blocked) saying vlSIFT beats Lowe's SIFT and OpenSIFT in execution time and keypoint count, but the snippet gave no figures; OpenCV answers threads give only anecdotes. Directional claim without numbers.

name: Vorbis
listed_description: Ogg Vorbis is a fully open, non-proprietary, patent-and-royalty-free, general-purpose compressed audio format.
reason: Reference codec library (xiph/vorbis). README and CHANGES (1.3.7, 1.3.6 and earlier) contain no speed or size comparison numbers; xiph.org pages are unreachable here; xiph/tremor has no README on its default branch to check. No numeric comparison against a named baseline found.

name: VTK
listed_description: Open-source, freely available software system for 3D computer graphics, image processing and visualization.
reason: Only reachable VTK evidence is self-referential or unquantified. vtkFlyingEdges3D.h/2D.h cite the Flying Edges paper (Schroeder, Maynard, Geveci, LDAV 2015) without numbers; the numeric tables (Kitware blog 'Really Fast Isocontouring', the vtk-developers 2015 announcement, the arXiv Parallel SurfaceNets paper 2401.14906) sit on blocked hosts and WebSearch snippets gave only 'one to two orders of magnitude faster than marching cubes' with an unconfirmed 2-5x serial figure. Release notes (Documentation/release/9.x.md and the 9.4 delimited-text-reader note: 0.873 s to 0.344 s) compare VTK against its own earlier versions, not another implementation. README has no performance claim.

name: x265
reason: Repo docs (readme.rst, introduction.rst, presets.rst, cli.rst, threading.rst on bitbucket raw) state goals and preset trade-offs but give no fps or speedup numbers against x264, HM or a platform codec. Independent speed comparisons exist (APSIPA 2014 SJTU evaluation, EUSIPCO 2017 citing HM as up to 1000x slower, forum fps tables) but their hosts (medialab.sjtu.edu.cn, eurasip.org, doom9, videohelp, x265.org, videolan.org) are unreachable here, and the snippets gave no usable figures. x265's own headline claim is compression efficiency, not speed.
